references.text: Their own eyes saw what the Lord did at Baal-Peor, how he destroyed all who followed Baal-Peor. A similar appeal to the eyewitness experience of the Lord's deeds.
Moses reminds the people of the great trials their eyes witnessed, the signs and wonders. The same theme of being eyewitnesses to the Lord's mighty works.
Moses refers to the great trials, signs, and wonders that the people's eyes had seen. A parallel to the eyewitness experience of the Lord's powerful deeds.
At the Sea of Reeds, Moses urged the people to see the Lord's salvation. This was one of the great deeds their eyes had witnessed.
Joshua reminds the people that they have seen everything the Lord their God has done to all these nations. The same theme of being eyewitnesses to the Lord's works.
Joshua speaks of how the people's eyes saw what the Lord did in Egypt. A direct parallel to the eyewitness testimony of the Lord's great deeds.
The psalmist invites us to come and see God's works, his awe-inspiring acts among humanity. The same theme of witnessing the Lord's great deeds.
